questions.ask: Does this app ship more than one language through next-intl?
questions.why: Yes installs the translation checks (key parity between catalogues, casing) and .claude/agent-config.json with localePairs, so post-edit tells the agent when one catalogue changed and its partner did not. A single-language app does not need them; check:i18n then prints a skip line and passes.
questions.detect: package.json depends on next-intl, or src/messages/*.json holds two or more catalogues

questions.ask: Does the app use dialogs (a Radix or shadcn Dialog, or a native <dialog>)?
questions.why: Yes installs the dialog-content rule, its standard and check:dialog-desc, which fails when a dialog has no announced description. Without dialogs the check has nothing to read; it then prints a skip line and passes.
questions.detect: package.json depends on @radix-ui/react-dialog, a components/ui/dialog.tsx exists, or a .tsx file renders <dialog

questions.ask: Adopt the responsive-layout module: named breakpoints and fluid widths, checked by check:responsive?
questions.why: It fails a pixel breakpoint, a class with no consumer, and a fixed width with no fluid guard, which is how a screen breaks at a width nobody opened. It reads src/styles/globals.css and the class prefixes listed at the top of scripts/check/responsive.ts, so a repo without that stylesheet answers no.

questions.ask: Does the app draw loading skeletons that must match the screen they stand in for?
questions.why: Yes installs the skeleton rule, its standard and check:skeleton-switch, which fails when the preview switch that shows a skeleton on purpose is left on. The agent-fe-nextjs:skeleton skill works from those files. An app without skeletons answers no.
questions.detect: files named *-skeleton.tsx or loading.tsx exist under src/

questions.ask: Run React Doctor on pull requests (advisory review comments and a commit status; it never fails the check)?
questions.why: Installs .github/workflows/react-doctor.yml, which runs the vendor's action pinned to one commit, with write access to pull-request comments and statuses. The action runs the CLI with its own defaults, which report diagnostics to the vendor's score service; the local react-doctor skill passes --no-score instead. Answer yes only if that is acceptable for this repo.
questions.detect: .github/workflows/react-doctor.yml already exists, or the user has asked for React Doctor in CI

questions.ask: Review each pull request with DeepSeek, a low-cost paid AI model (.github/workflows/deepseek-review.yml)?
questions.why: Installs a caller of agent-config-kit's reusable DeepSeek review, with notes about this stack: one comment per pull request from a branch of this repository, updated when the repository's owner, a member or a collaborator comments /ask-deepseek. It reads the diff over the GitHub API and runs no pull-request code. It needs the repository secret DEEPSEEK_API_KEY and costs about ten US cents a review at most, usually a cent or two (the diff and the answer are capped); without the secret it passes and sends nothing.
questions.detect: .github/workflows/deepseek-review.yml already exists, or the user has asked for an AI review in CI

questions.ask: Will you use the impeccable design skill (installed separately, by reference) and want its PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md templates?
questions.why: Adds PRODUCT.example.md and DESIGN.example.md at the repo root, the product and visual-system files that skill reads. They are templates to fill in and rename; without the skill they are clutter.
questions.detect: skills-lock.json or .claude/skills/ names impeccable, or PRODUCT.md or DESIGN.md exists

questions.ask: Seal request and response bodies between the browser, this app's server and the backend (the payload contract: encrypted envelopes, one endpoint registry, checked before merge)?
questions.why: Yes installs the payload contract: a reference implementation in src/lib/payload/ (AES-256-GCM envelopes bound to method, route and status; pre-shared key rings; browser key agreement; the browser transport and the proxy bridge; the strict/off switch) with its tests at 100%, the endpoint registry and its generator, check:endpoints (registry drift, route literals, reasons, the committed switch) and check:crypto-interop (the shared test vectors, and peers checked out beside this repo), the contract document and a rule that loads when you touch the transport. Wiring it into the app stays yours: the contract document shows where. No new dependency (WebCrypto). Answer no when bodies need no sealing beyond TLS.
questions.detect: payload.config.json or src/lib/payload/ already exists, or the backend this app calls expects sealed bodies

packageScripts.fl: bun run format && bun run lint
packageScripts.check:i18n: if [ -f scripts/check/i18n.ts ]; then bun run scripts/check/i18n.ts && bun run scripts/check/i18n-casing.ts; else echo 'check:i18n skipped: setup did not install the i18n module'; fi
packageScripts.check:dialog-desc: if [ -f scripts/check/dialog-desc.ts ]; then bun run scripts/check/dialog-desc.ts; else echo 'check:dialog-desc skipped: setup did not install the dialogs module'; fi
packageScripts.check:responsive: if [ -f scripts/check/responsive.ts ]; then bun run scripts/check/responsive.ts; else echo 'check:responsive skipped: setup did not install the responsive module'; fi
packageScripts.check:skeleton-switch: if [ -f scripts/check/skeleton-switch.sh ]; then bash scripts/check/skeleton-switch.sh; else echo 'check:skeleton-switch skipped: setup did not install the skeletons module'; fi
packageScripts.check:skeleton-pairs: if [ -f scripts/check/skeleton-pairs.ts ]; then bun run scripts/check/skeleton-pairs.ts; else echo 'check:skeleton-pairs skipped: setup did not install the skeletons module'; fi
packageScripts.check:endpoints: if [ -f scripts/check/endpoints.ts ]; then bun run scripts/check/endpoints.ts; else echo 'check:endpoints skipped: setup did not install the payload module'; fi
packageScripts.check:crypto-interop: if [ -f scripts/check/crypto-interop.ts ]; then bun run scripts/check/crypto-interop.ts; else echo 'check:crypto-interop skipped: setup did not install the payload module'; fi
